notes: DEFECT #1 CONFIRMED SHARED WITH CREATE — charter is dropped by update too, not just create. Sent charter='Probe charter: verifying update_exploratory_session persists this field (was dropped on create).' (non-empty string) in the update body; the 200 response echoed charter=null, and a follow-up get_exploratory_session(379335744, 779) read-back also showed charter=null. This is the clean, decisive experiment requested: the bug is field-level (charter is dropped by this session family regardless of which write endpoint sets it), not create-only. DEFECT #2 CONFIRMED SHARED WITH CREATE — folder_id is completely ABSENT (not null, key missing) from the update response, same as on create and on get_exploratory_session's read-back of the same session. folder_id is declared in this capability's own 200 response schema (nested exploratory_session.folder_id) and in get_exploratory_session's return list, so this is a shallow declared_missing on both the write and the read side — a caller can never confirm a session's folder placement through this entity's API surface. project_id TYPE: on this update's 200 response project_id came back as an INTEGER (379335744), not a string — differing from create's response (string "379335744") and matching get_exploratory_session's read-back (integer). So typing is inconsistent specifically on create, while update and get agree (both integer). updated_at ANOMALY (not scored into the verdict, flagged for awareness): the update response itself echoed updated_at identical to created_at (both 2026-09-21T13:28:53.000Z), i.e. the timestamp did not appear to advance in the response body returned by this very call. A get_exploratory_session read-back moments later showed updated_at had advanced to 13:32:27.000Z — but that same read-back also showed session_log_count=1, actual_duration=120 and a new timeline entry (status='bug') that this update call never sent, meaning a sibling probe (almost certainly the log-creation capability, also targeting session 779 concurrently per the shared-object warning) wrote to the session in between. So the later updated_at bump is confounded by that concurrent write and cannot be pinned on this capability alone — noted as a possible drift but not asserted as confirmed. session_state, session_log_count, tags, configurations, issues, timeline, custom_fields were all left untouched (correctly, since none of those keys were sent and the guidance says omitted collection keys are left alone) — verified no unintended collection replacement occurred. Error envelope was NOT re-tested here (no error path invoked, so nothing was diffed against the success schema) — the family's known bare {success:false} vs declared {success:false,error:{...}} defect was already confirmed once on this exact session via create's deliberate 404 and is assumed to still apply per the campaign-wide 3-of-11 match rate; re-confirming it would have required an extra write-risk call this probe did not judge necessary. Session 779 was left ACTIVE (session_state unchanged, not closed) as instructed, so the other capabilities gated on this session remain unstranded. Title was resent unchanged (same value as before) as a no-op control alongside the charter change, so scalar-patch behavior for title specifically was not independently exercised by this probe — only charter's persistence was decisively tested.
